verbs: Walking the One Ring to Mordor

tips: A wizard is never late. Nor is he early. He arrives precisely when he means to.
Avoid the Old Forest, and if you can't, sing for Tom Bombadil.
Do not meddle in the affairs of wizards, for they are subtle and quick to anger.
Don't forget second breakfast! It's the second most important meal of the day.
Don't take the Paths of the Dead without an army of your own.
Don't throw stones in the lake! You might wake the Watcher in the Water.
Elevenses, luncheon, afternoon tea, dinner, and supper also matter. Plan accordingly.
Even the smallest person can change the course of the future.
Fly, you fool!
If you put on the Ring you may be invisible to most, but the Nazgûl will see you!
Keep it secret. Keep it safe.
Mithril is light as a feather and hard as dragon scales. Wear it under your coat.
Never laugh at live dragons.
Never toss a dwarf. Exceptions apply.
Never trust a talking spider. Or anyone who calls you 'precious'.
Not all those who wander are lost.
One does not simply walk into Mordor. Pack lembas.
Po-tay-toes: boil 'em, mash 'em, stick 'em in a stew.
Short cuts make long delays. Stay on the road.
Speak 'friend' and enter. Read riddles carefully.
When in doubt, follow your nose. Or a Ranger.
When the beacons are lit, Rohan will answer. Usually.
